value.name: Mandatory prepayment / events of default

value.value: Mandatory prepayment (Section 2.17): if Total Outstandings cause Availability to be less than zero, prepay to eliminate deficiency plus 103% cash collateral of L/C Outstandings; daily repayment under Section 2.18 during Cash Dominion Event; Net Proceeds from a Prepayment Event applied per Section 7.03. value.agreement_title: SECOND AMENDED AND RESTATED CREDIT AGREEMENT

value.name: Mandatory prepayment / events of default

value.value: Mandatory Prepayment (SECTION 2.17): If Total Outstandings causes Availability to be less than zero, Borrowers will immediately prepay Revolving Credit Loans to eliminate the deficiency and, if necessary, deposit cash into the Cash Collateral Account equal to 103% of the Letters of Credit Outstanding. Events of Default (SECTION 7.01): include (a) failure to pay principal/reimbursement obligations; (b) failure to pay interest, fees or other amounts (5 Business Day grace); (c) incorrect representation or warranty; (d)-(e) failure to observe covenants; (f) cross-default to Material Indebtedness; (g) Change in Control; (h)-(i) involuntary/voluntary insolvency proceedings; (k) final judgments in excess of $75,000,000; (l) ERISA Event; (m)-(n) challenges to Loan Document validity; (o) Lien ceasing to be valid and perfected; (p) termination of Facility Guarantee.
value.note: verbatim: “SECTION 2.17 Mandatory Prepayment; Commitment Termination; Cash Collateral . The outstanding Obligations shall be subject to prepayment as follows: (a) If at any time the Total Outstandings causes Availability to be less than zero, the Borrowers will, immediately upon notice from the Administrative Agent: (x) prepay the Revolving Credit Loans in an amount necessary to eliminate such deficiency; and (y) if, after giving effect to the prepayment in full of all outstanding Revolving Credit Loans such deficiency has not been eliminated, deposit cash into the Cash Collateral Account in an amount equal to 103% of the Letters of Credit Outstanding.”
